props.title: Ensemble sizes for a Colorado Springs party.
props.lede: A duo sounds great from anywhere in your venue, and the two musicians don’t take up much space.

props.html: One voice and a guitar is a lovely choice for a small dinner or an outdoor afternoon.

It’s the size we book most often in Colorado Springs. You can choose voice and guitar if you’d like songs your guests can sing along to, or guitar and upright bass if you’d like to keep it instrumental through dinner.
If you’re planning on dancing, a trio can get people moving, and you won’t have to find a stage for it.

props.title: Private party venues in Colorado Springs

props.html: Private celebrations in The Springs tend to happen at a handful of great places. Garden of the Gods Resort and Club and Cheyenne Mountain Resort are popular for family gatherings and milestone weekends, and both have lovely terraces for drinks before dinner. The Broadmoor is on a bigger scale, and it hosts plenty of large events. Downtown, The Mining Exchange and The Antlers work well if you’d like your guests to be able to walk over from their hotel.

In our experience, weddings are an even bigger part of the event calendar in The Springs than in Denver, and a wedding weekend comes with plenty of parties, too. A duo is an excellent choice for the Friday welcome party, the rehearsal dinner or the Sunday brunch. Planning the wedding day itself? Check out live music for Colorado Springs weddings, from the ceremony to the dance floor.
A party at home is often even easier for us to plan. You usually won’t need a stage. Just tell us the address and which door to use, and we’ll plan how to bring in the gear ahead of time.

props.title: Planning an outdoor party in Colorado Springs

props.html: Colorado Springs sits at about 6,035 feet, and guests from sea level may notice it, but it doesn’t change anything for our musicians. The bigger thing to plan for in The Springs is the weather. Wind can come off the range, and a terrace can get about fifteen degrees cooler as the sun goes down, so we’ll work out a plan with you ahead of time for moving indoors.
We also play private parties in Denver and Boulder, and if you’re planning a company party in The Springs, take a look at our Colorado Springs holiday party page.

items.q: Do your musicians travel from Denver to Colorado Springs?
items.a: Yes, Signet Artists is based in Denver, and our musicians are happy to make the drive down I-25. The band can usually drive home the same night, so you won’t need to think about lodging. Wondering what live music costs along the Front Range? Take a look at our Live Music Cost Guide.

items.q: Can a band play outdoors on a Colorado Springs terrace?
items.a: Yes, as long as the spot is covered, level and dry and there’s power nearby. If the weather starts to turn, we’ll talk with you early about moving the music inside.

items.q: What does a band need to set up in Colorado Springs?
items.a: A solo musician can usually fit in about 6 by 4 feet, a duo in a corner of about 8 by 6 and a trio in about 12 by 8. A duo will usually need one outlet that isn’t sharing power with anything else. Setup can take 45 to 60 minutes. If a club or resort asks for a certificate of insurance, just let us know.
